question: A company trained a text-generation large language model (LLM). The company must use a human evaluation method to evaluate the model's performance. Which human evaluation methods will meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

options.text: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
options.explanation: ROUGE is an automatic evaluation metric that measures overlap between generated text and reference text. ROUGE is not a human evaluation method.

options.text: Likert scale - comparison
options.explanation: You can use Likert scale - comparison for human evaluation. In this method, a human evaluator indicates a preference between two responses. In contrast, Likert scale - individual uses a human evaluator to indicate how strongly the evaluator approves of the model responses on a scale of five points.

options.text: Factual knowledge
options.explanation: Factual knowledge is an automatic evaluation method for open-ended text generation tasks. However, this method is not the most suitable metric for human evaluation.

options.text: Semantic robustness
options.explanation: Semantic robustness is an automated model evaluation method for text summarization models. Semantic robustness does not include human evaluators. Semantic robustness is a measure of quality of the model's text summary changes in response to small, semantic-preserving changes. However, the model in the scenario is a text-generation model.

options.text: Ordinal rank
options.explanation: You can use ordinal rank for human evaluation. A human evaluator will rank preferred responses to a prompt in order, starting at "1". The evaluator must use the instructions provided to understand the definition of "1". In the final report, the results display as a histogram of the evaluators' rankings over the whole dataset.

question: An ML engineer launched an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance with the default configuration. The SageMaker notebook will train and deploy a new model with the tools and libraries available in SageMaker AI. The ML engineer successfully deploys the model. Then, the ML engineer receives a high-severity security alert that says the ML engineer should not have administrator privileges to the SageMaker notebook instances. The ML engineer must remediate the security issue while following best practices. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable encryption of the Amazon EBS volumes that are attached to the notebook instance.
options.explanation: To encrypt EBS volumes that are attached to notebook instances is a security best practice to provide additional security to the volume. However, the scenario requires you to remediate root access to users. A solution that encrypts EBS volumes does not restrict root access to the notebook instance.

options.text: Redeploy the SageMaker notebook instance into an Amazon VPC.
options.explanation: When you launch a notebook instance in an Amazon VPC, you can limit access to the notebook instance at the network layer. This solution gives you the ability to limit internet connectivity to prevent malicious code or public libraries from accessing the data. However, the scenario requires you to remediate root access to users. This solution does not restrict root access to the notebook instance. When you create a SageMaker notebook instance with the default configuration, users that log in to the instance have root access. This type of access allows users to install tools and packages.

options.text: Update the SageMaker notebook instance to disable root access.
options.explanation: To disable root access on the SageMaker notebook instance will prevent unintended privilege elevation. This solution follows the recommended security best practice to restrict root access where access is not explicitly necessary. You can perform this action by changing the RootAccess setting to Disabled for the notebook instance when you create an update of the notebook instance.

options.text: Restrict inbound traffic to the SageMaker notebook instance security group.
options.explanation: Traffic limits access to the notebook instance at the network layer. However, the scenario requires you to remediate root access to the ML engineer. This solution does not restrict root access to the notebook instance.

question: A financial services company created a feature group in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. The feature group manages user-related ML features across different areas. Data has already been loaded into SageMaker Feature Store. An ML engineer needs to add a new feature to the feature group. The feature group will be used in several ML marketing models. The ML engineer must update the historical records to include the values of the new feature. Which combination of steps should the ML engineer take to add the new feature? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use the UpdateFeatureGroup operation to add the new feature to the feature group. Specify the name and type.
options.explanation: A SageMaker feature group gives you the ability to add new features through the UpdateFeatureGroup operation. When you use this API, you need to provide the new feature names and types.

options.text: Use the PutRecord operation to overwrite the records that do not have data for the new feature.
options.explanation: A SageMaker feature group gives you the ability to overwrite previous records through the PutRecord operation. When you use this API, you can overwrite the historical records that do not include data for the recently added feature.

options.text: Delete all previous records from the feature group.
options.explanation: A SageMaker feature group gives you the ability to overwrite previous records through the PutRecord operation. You do not need to delete the previous historical records from the feature group to overwrite the records. Therefore, this step is not necessary to add the new feature.

options.explanation: A SageMaker feature group gives you the ability to add new features after you create the feature group. However, you do not need to delete the feature group to add the new feature. Therefore, this step is not necessary to add the new feature.

options.text: Use the CreateFeatureGroup operation to create a new feature group with the updated features. Specify the name and type.
options.explanation: A SageMaker feature group gives you the ability to add new features after you create the feature group. However, you do not need to create a new feature group to add the new feature. Therefore, this step is not necessary to add the new feature.

question: A company wants to predict the number of product units that will be sold for the next year. The company wants to create an ML model that is based on historical sales data by using Amazon SageMaker AI. This dataset has previously been labeled. Which algorithm should the company use to create the model?

options.text: Logistic regression
options.explanation: Logistic regression algorithm is a supervised algorithm that is used to classify a data point between two different classes. In this scenario, the company wants a predicted value, not to label data in two different classes. Therefore, this option does not meet the requirements.

options.text: K-means
options.explanation: The k-means algorithm is an unsupervised algorithm that is used for grouping data points based on a chosen attribute. The scenario does not require this solution because the company does not need to label data.

options.text: DeepAR
options.explanation: The DeepAR algorithm is a supervised algorithm that is used to forecast time-series prediction by using recurrent neural networks (RNN). In this scenario, the company wants to forecast the number of units that they are going to sell. Therefore, this algorithm can be used to achieve the expected results.

options.text: Random Cut Forest (RCF)
options.explanation: The RCF algorithm is an unsupervised algorithm that is used for detecting anomalous data points within a dataset. In this scenario, the company wants to predict the number of units sold for a product, not to detect irregular data points. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirements.

question: An ML engineer wants to train a model to analyze customer turnover in a telecommunications company. The training code requires access to third-party Python libraries including scikit-learn, NumPy, pandas, and a proprietary library. options.text: Use a SageMaker AI built-in algorithm to run the training job.

options.explanation: The scikit-learn framework container is a prebuilt image that SageMaker AI provides. options.text: Build and push a custom container with the necessary Python dependencies to Amazon ECR. Run the training job by using the container image.

options.text: Use the prebuilt SageMaker AI scikit-learn framework container to run the training job.

The scikit-learn framework container installs the scikit-learn Python module for ML workloads. However, the prebuilt container does not include the proprietary library that you need for the training script. Therefore, you cannot successfully run the script by using this container.

question: An ML engineer developed a PyTorch model and a TensorFlow model. The ML engineer wants to deploy the models by using Amazon SageMaker AI. The models will be accessed individually. The models need to serve traffic with low latency. Which deployment option will meet these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference to create a multi-model endpoint with built-in containers.
options.explanation: SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference is an inference option that you can use for real-time, low-latency use cases. Multi-model endpoints provide a scalable and cost-effective way to deploy many models. Multi-model endpoints use the same fleet of resources and a shared serving container to host all your models. SageMaker AI provides prebuilt Docker containers for PyTorch and TensorFlow. However, a multi-model endpoint requires all the models to use the same ML framework. Because the models use two different frameworks, a multi-model endpoint is not suitable for this use case.

options.text: Use SageMaker AI Serverless Inference to create two on-demand serverless endpoints by using a custom Docker container for each model.
options.explanation: SageMaker AI Serverless Inference is an inference option that you can use to deploy ML models without the need to provision or manage infrastructure. On-demand serverless inference is suitable for workloads that have idle periods between traffic spurts and that can tolerate cold starts. SageMaker AI supports using custom container images. However, on-demand serverless inference is not suitable to serve low-latency requests. For workloads that cannot tolerate cold starts, you should use provisioned concurrency with serverless inference or SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference.

options.text: Use SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference to create a multi-model endpoint by using a custom Docker container for each model.
options.explanation: SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference is an inference option that you can use for real-time, low-latency use cases. SageMaker AI supports using custom container images. However, a multi-model endpoint requires all models to use the same ML framework. Because the models use two different frameworks, a multi-model endpoint is not suitable for this use case.

options.text: Use SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference to create a multi-container endpoint with direct invocation.
options.explanation: SageMaker AI Real-Time Inference is an inference option that you can use for real-time, low-latency use cases. You can use SageMaker AI multi-container endpoints to deploy multiple containers that use different models or frameworks on a single SageMaker AI endpoint. You can run the containers in a sequence as an inference pipeline. Alternatively, you can access each container individually by using direct invocation to improve endpoint utilization and to optimize costs.

question: An ML engineer must collect and transform application logs that are stored in Amazon CloudWatch. The application logs will be used in a training dataset. The JSON-formatted logs can be retrieved by using a CloudWatch subscription filter. The logs must be aggregated in Apache Parquet format and stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use an Amazon SQS to collect the logs. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to implement conversion to Parquet.
options.explanation: Amazon SQS offers a secure and durable queue that you can use to integrate and decouple distributed software systems and the system's components. For this solution, you must create an Amazon SQS queue. Therefore, this solution adds operational overhead. Additionally, this solution requires you to configure and manually implement a Lambda function to perform the record conversion.

options.text: Use Amazon Data Firehose to collect the logs and configure output conversion to Parquet.
options.explanation: Firehose is a fully managed service that can deliver real-time streaming data to various destinations, including Amazon S3. This solution requires you to configure a Firehose stream that converts data to the target format and stores the data to an S3 bucket. Therefore, this solution requires the least operational overhead.

options.text: Use an AWS Lambda function to collect the logs and implement conversion to Parquet.
options.explanation: Lambda is a serverless service that you can use to run code without the need to configure or provision the underlying infrastructure. This solution requires you to create a Lambda function and to write code within the Lambda function. Therefore, this solution requires additional operational overhead.

options.text: Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to collect the logs. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to load the data and implement conversion to Parquet.
options.explanation: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database. For this solution, you must create a DynamoDB table. To manage the table requires additional operational overhead. Additionally, you must configure and manually implement a Lambda function to perform the record conversion. You cannot configure DynamoDB as a CloudWatch subscription filter.

question: An ML engineer must build a data engineering pipeline for a company. The pipeline must perform pre-processing steps to measure and monitor the quality of ingested data from custom sources. The pipeline will support terabyte-size workloads for each batch. The pipeline must integrate with the company's existing ML pipeline. The solution must require minimal operational management. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function. Create Python code. Run the Lambda function to measure the quality of the data.
options.explanation: Lambda is a serverless service that you can use to run code without providing or managing infrastructure. Lambda has a runtime quota of 15 minutes. Therefore, Lambda is not suitable for processing long-running tasks such as ETL jobs. You cannot ensure that Lambda will be able to process terabyte-size workloads for each batch within 15 minutes.

options.text: Create an AWS Glue DataBrew job. Run the DataBrew job to measure the quality of the data.
options.explanation: DataBrew serves as a no-code data preparation tool to help with data cleaning and normalization processes. DataBrew can help reduce data preparation time. However, this solution is not the most operationally efficient method to monitor the quality of ingested data simultaneously. This solution requires additional effort to define the ruleset, integrate with AWS Glue jobs, and generate relevant events for monitoring purposes.

options.text: Provision an Amazon EMR cluster. Create PySpark code. Run the PySpark code to measure the quality of the data.
options.explanation: Amazon EMR is a managed cluster platform that you can use to run big data frameworks for efficient data processing and analysis. Provisioning an EMR cluster requires additional configuration to set up, deploy, and maintain the cluster. Additionally, you must write PySpark code to measure the data's quality. Therefore, this solution requires additional development effort and ongoing maintenance of the code.

options.text: Create an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job by using AWS Glue. Integrate AWS Glue Data Quality rulesets to measure the quality of the data.
options.explanation: AWS Glue is a data integration service that you can use to discover, prepare, and integrate data from various sources. Data Quality is a feature of AWS Glue that you can use to measure and monitor data quality. You can use Data Quality to enhance overall data reliability and integrity. You can define rulesets and integrate the rulesets with an AWS Glue ETL job. Then, the rulesets can measure and monitor the quality of the data. This solution provides the least development effort because rulesets are available within Data Quality.

question: A multinational company develops specialized natural language processing (NLP) capabilities by fine-tuning a foundation model (FM). The company uses Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for seven distinct business domains. Now, the company needs a production deployment solution. The solution must minimize costs. The solution must maintain sub-second latency for concurrent requests across different domains. The solution must support dynamic loading of different LoRA adapters based on the incoming request context. Which Amazon SageMaker AI deployment solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Deploy separate endpoints for each domain-specific LoRA-adapted model.
options.explanation: This solution provides isolation between models and helps with troubleshooting. However, this solution is less cost-effective because you need separate compute resources for each model.

options.text: Deploy a single multi-container endpoint. Set the mode setting equal to direct in the model configuration.
options.explanation: This solution provides multiple containers on the same endpoint. However, this solution duplicates the base model in memory. This solution does not take advantage of LoRA's shared base model approach.

options.text: Deploy a single endpoint that uses inference components. Specify the FM as BaseInferenceComponent.
options.explanation: This solution dynamically loads lightweight LoRA adapters. This solution maintains only one copy of the base model in memory. Therefore, this solution reduces infrastructure costs and is the most cost-effective.

options.text: Deploy a single multi-model endpoint. Set the mode setting to multi-model on the container.
options.explanation: A SageMaker AI multi-model endpoint supports multiple models. However, a multi-model endpoint is designed for separate models. This solution duplicates the base model in memory. This solution does not take advantage of LoRA's shared base model approach.

question: A company wants to use Amazon Bedrock to automatically generate customer-facing content. The content must concisely explain the company's operational rules, special events, and guidelines. All content that is generated by Amazon Bedrock must be consistent with the company's brand guidelines. The company plans to use the Claude family of models by Anthropic on Amazon Bedrock. Which combination of model configuration adjustments will meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

options.text: Control length by using max_tokens_to_sample (int).
options.explanation: The max_tokens_to_sample parameter provides direct control over the length of the generated text. You can use this parameter to ensure that the output is brief and ends at an appropriate length. This parameter is useful for creating concise messages that need to match information like operational rules, special events, and brand guidelines.

options.text: Use higher top_k (int).
options.explanation: A higher top_k value increases the pool of considered words, potentially leading to more varied outputs. The company wants to generate concise, consistent messages that match specific brand guidelines and operational information. Increasing the top_k value could cause generated text to be too varied, not follow brand guidelines, or be irrelevant.

options.text: Use higher temperature (float).
options.explanation: A higher temperature value increases the randomness and creativity of the model. The company wants to generate concise, consistent messages that match specific brand guidelines and operational information. Increasing the temperature setting could cause the generated text to be too varied, not follow brand guidelines, or be irrelevant.

options.text: Use higher top_p (float).
options.explanation: A higher top_p value can lead to more varied and unpredictable outputs. A higher top_p value is not recommended to generate concise, consistent messages that need to match specific brand guidelines and operational information. This solution increases the risk that the generated text could be too varied, not follow brand guidelines, or be irrelevant.

options.text: Use specific stop_sequences (string).
options.explanation: The stop_sequences parameter provides the precise marking of content endpoints. By using clear endpoints, the generated content remains organized and consistent. This parameter can match the company's brand guidelines.

question: An AI engineer must implement a solution that processes hundreds of thousands of text inputs once every 24 hours. Each of the inputs is inserted into a prompt and sent to a large language model (LLM) for inference. The LLM response must be stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow that invokes an AWS Lambda function for each input. In the Lambda function, run single-prompt inference by using Amazon Bedrock LLMs and store the result in Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Step Functions is a serverless orchestration service that you can use to create a series of event-driven steps in a workflow. This solution requires you to create a Step Functions workflow and a Lambda function. Therefore, this solution requires additional operational overhead.

options.text: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow that calls an InvokeModel action for Amazon Bedrock for each input. Add a step to the workflow that stores the result in Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Step Functions is a serverless orchestration service that you can use to create a series of event-driven steps in a workflow. Amazon Bedrock gives you the ability to experiment with and evaluate top foundational models for your use case. When you use Amazon Bedrock, you do not need to manage any infrastructure. However, this solution requires you to create a Step Functions workflow and a Lambda function. Additionally, this solution requires the Step Functions step to store the result in Amazon S3. Therefore, this solution requires additional operational overhead.

options.text: Create a batch inference job in Amazon Bedrock. Specify the input file as an input to a CreateModelInvocationJob request. Copy the output of the job to the target S3 bucket.
options.explanation: To create a batch inference job, you need to send a CreateModelInvocationJob request in Amazon Bedrock. The CreateModelInvocationJob request does not accept inputs as files and does not return outputs as files. Instead, the CreateModelInvocationJob request accepts two S3 locations as input parameters, one to read input data from and one to store outputs to.

options.text: Create a batch inference job in Amazon Bedrock. Store the input file in an S3 bucket and specify the stored file as an input to a CreateModelInvocationJob request. Specify the output location for the request as the target S3 bucket.

The CreateModelInvocationJob request will read the inputs from a location in an S3 bucket. The file needs to be in JSONL format and should have one input request on each line. options.text: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) algorithm

options.text: Linear learner algorithm

options.text: Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm

question: A logistics company is using Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-powered shipment tracking application. A development team creates a set of prompts in Amazon Bedrock that generate estimated delivery updates for customers. The development team needs to compare the prompts to ensure that the final prompt can be reliably used in the production shipment tracking application without being accidentally modified. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

options.text: Create multiple prompt variants in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management. Configure each variant with a different model and inference parameters. Use the compare variants feature to evaluate outputs side by side.

options.text: Select the highest performing variant. Create a version of the prompt in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management. Create a snapshot that the production application can reference.

options.text: Select the highest performing variant. Use the UpdatePrompt API to update the prompt in Amazon Bedrock Flows.

options.text: Create multiple prompts in Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management for each model configuration. Use an Amazon Bedrock model evaluation job to compare outputs. Use automated metrics to score the outputs.
options.explanation: Model evaluation jobs can assess model outputs against automated metrics such as toxicity and accuracy. options.text: Select the highest performing variant. Use the Amazon Bedrock prompt optimization feature to select the model and inference parameters that the production application can reference.
options.explanation: Optimization rewrites prompts to yield inference results that are more suitable for your use case. Optimization does not compare the prompts.

question: An ML engineer is training a large deep learning model on Amazon SageMaker AI. The full training run takes several hours to complete. Based on the current configuration, any disruptions to the training job requires restarting the entire training from the beginning. The ML engineer wants to implement a solution to better handle the interruptions during training. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.text: Use checkpoints in SageMaker AI to automatically save model artifacts to Amazon S3 at regular intervals during training.
options.explanation: You can use checkpoints to capture the state of a model during training in SageMaker AI. Then you can resume the training from the last checkpoint. You can use this solution to avoid restarting the training process from the beginning if the training fails or is interrupted. Checkpoints are an operationally efficient and automated way to resume training at the last saved checkpoint.

options.text: Use SageMaker Autopilot to automatically handle model training and save intermediate results.
options.explanation: SageMaker Autopilot is an automated ML service that handles the complete ML workflow from data preprocessing to model deployment. SageMaker Autopilot manages the training process, but does not provide specific checkpoint functionality for handling training interruptions. SageMaker Autopilot focuses on automating model creation and tuning, not on managing training state persistence.

options.text: Create an additional module in the training flow to save copies of the model to Amazon S3 at set intervals by using custom training code.
options.explanation: You can manually save model artifacts to Amazon S3 during training. You can use this solution to restart from a previous manually saved point. However, this solution involves custom development. Therefore, this solution is not operationally efficient compared to checkpoints that automate the process.

options.text: Use SageMaker Model Cards to capture intermediate snapshots of the model state during training.
options.explanation: SageMaker Model Cards provide a centralized location to document critical details about ML models. You would typically use SageMaker Model Cards for governance and reporting. You cannot use SageMaker Model Cards to capture intermediate snapshots of data during the training process.

question: A company is working to improve its customer service platform. The company has gathered a large dataset composed of customer cases, emails, and chat. An ML associate must use a built-in algorithm that is available in Amazon SageMaker AI to generate relevant summaries of the customer interaction data to service specialists. Which algorithm should the associate use to develop this solution?

options.text: Use the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) algorithm.
options.explanation: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is an algorithm that finds patterns in the words that are used across documents to help you uncover the most relevant topics associated with them. The LDA algorithm can predict how similar documents are based on the frequency of similar words, and can be used to recommend documents based on similar topics. However, the LDA algorithm will not generate the text summaries needed for this scenario. Instead, you should use an algorithm with text summarization capabilities, such as seq2seq.

options.text: Use the semantic segmentation algorithm.
options.explanation: Semantic segmentation is an image analysis algorithm, not a text analysis algorithm. The algorithm has pixel-level capabilities that can be used to develop computer vision solutions, such as sensors in robots or self-driving vehicles. The scenario requires an algorithm with text analysis capabilities to generate the summaries, such as seq2seq.

options.text: Use the Sequence-to-Sequence (seq2seq) algorithm.
options.explanation: Sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) is an algorithm that uses sequences of tokens, such as text, as an input and produces new sequences of tokens as the output. An example of the seq2seq algorithm capabilities is the one needed for the scenario to generate text summaries. The input will be a longer stream of tokens (words from the text) that the company has gathered from their customer service history of interactions. The predicted output will be a shorter stream of words that will represent a summary of the input. The company then will be able to use the generated summaries to develop the new customer service application.

options.text: Use the BlazingText algorithm to apply Word2vec embeddings.
options.explanation: BlazingText is an algorithm that provides implementations of two different text analysis algorithms: Word2vec and Text Classification. Using Word2vec maps words into vectors or word-embeddings that are similar from a semantical point of view. Although Word2vec embeddings can be used to organize datasets into topics by creating word groupings, it will not provide text summaries like the ones needed for this scenario. Instead, you should use an algorithm with text summarization capabilities, such as seq2seq.

question: A company stores both unstructured and structured text data in an Amazon S3 bucket. options.text: Use AWS Batch to extract, transform, and load (ETL) the data. Use Amazon RDS to process SQL queries.
options.explanation: AWS Batch provisions compute resources. AWS Batch optimizes job distribution based on the volume and resource requirements of the job. However, if you use AWS Batch, you must define compute resources. Amazon RDS can perform SQL queries. However, you must load the data into a separate RDS database engine. Therefore, this solution requires additional operational overhead.

options.text: Process the data by using Apache Spark on Amazon EMR. Query the data by using SQL from a Jupyter notebook on the cluster.
options.explanation: You can use Amazon EMR to run Spark to process data in Amazon S3. A Jupyter notebook is a web-based integrated development environment (IDE) that you can use to work with code. This solution is technically feasible. However, building an EMR cluster of Amazon EC2 instances requires more operational overhead than using serverless services such as AWS Glue and Athena.

options.text: Catalog the data by using AWS Glue. Use Amazon Athena to run queries.
options.explanation: AWS Glue is a fully managed serverless ETL service. You can use AWS Glue to build a catalog to discover and prepare data for ML. Athena is a serverless SQL query service that you can use to query data that you catalog in AWS Glue.

options.text: Catalog the data by using Amazon Rekognition. Use Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 to process SQL queries.
options.explanation: You can use Amazon Rekognition for image and video analysis. You cannot use Amazon Rekognition to catalog text data. Aurora is a relational database service that you can use to perform SQL queries. However, you must process and load the data into a separate data store before you can use Aurora to query the data.

question: An AI engineer wants to use Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to automate the fine-tuning of a large language model (LLM). The LLM performs text summarization. The AI engineer must assess the quality of the fine-tuned model. Which evaluation metric should the AI engineer review on the completed AutoML job?

options.text: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU)
options.explanation: You can use BLEU to evaluate machine translation tasks. BLEU measures the precision of n-gram overlaps between generated and reference text. You would not use BLEU for text summarization fine-tuning.

options.text: Term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF)
options.explanation: TF-IDF is a statistical measure that you can use for information retrieval and text mining. TF-IDF evaluates the importance of a word in a document relative to a corpus. TF-IDF is not an evaluation metric for assessing the quality of text summarization models.

options.text: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE)
options.explanation: ROUGE is a set of metrics available in LLM fine-tuning AutoML jobs. ROUGE evaluates the quality of machine-generated text. This metric is the most suitable to use in this scenario. You can use ROUGE metrics to measure the similarity between machine-generated text and the ground truth text of a validation dataset.

options.text: Weighted quantile loss (wQL)
options.explanation: A time series forecasting AutoML job can capture the wQL metric to measure the accuracy of the forecast. However, you cannot use this metric in LLM fine-tuning AutoML jobs.

question: A company is building an ML model for demand forecasting by using a time series prediction model. The company stores 10 years of sales data in Amazon S3. Parquet format is suitable to store and process large datasets efficiently. Redshift Spectrum can use Parquet's columnar format to eliminate unnecessary columns from the scan. options.text: Convert the data to Avro format by using the Python SDK in AWS Lambda.
options.explanation: Lambda is a serverless computing service that you can use to run code without provisioning or managing servers. You can use Avro as an efficient binary format for serialization. Avro format is inefficient for analytical querying use cases such as demand forecasting that uses Redshift Spectrum. Columnar formats are more suitable to optimize query performance than Avro.

options.text: Convert the data to CSV format by using the Python SDK in AWS Lambda.
options.explanation: Lambda is a serverless computing service that you can use to run code without provisioning or managing servers. Lambda is not suitable for large-scale file conversion tasks because of memory and execution quotas. CSV format is text-based. Text-based file formats are not as high-performing as columnar formats in processing speed and storage space. The company stores a large volume of data on Amazon S3. Therefore, Parquet format provides better query performance than CSV format.

options.text: Convert the data to JSON format by using an AWS Glue job.
options.explanation: AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service. AWS Glue provides options to read and write various data formats. The JSON data format is designed for structuring data in a text-based format. Text-based file formats are not as high-performing as columnar formats in processing speed and storage space. question: A manufacturing company is monitoring vehicle entry and exit in real time by using car license plate tracking in a parking lot. A data science team created a proprietary computer vision model for automatic license plate recognition (ALPR). question: A company is starting a new ML learning project that will use Amazon SageMaker Studio. The company currently uses AWS ML services for several initiatives. question: An AI engineer needs to continuously assess the quality of an application's AI agent interactions in production. question: A company wants to deploy a generative AI (GenAI) application by using Amazon Bedrock. The company must customize a model for a specific use case. options.text: Continued pre-training

options.text: Model distillation

Then, the smaller model can achieve comparable accuracy for specific use cases.

options.text: Reinforcement fine-tuning
options.explanation: Reinforcement fine-tuning improves model alignment through feedback-based learning. Reinforcement fine-tuning does not specifically produce a smaller, faster model that achieves accuracy comparable to a larger model.

question: An AI engineer deploys a generative AI (GenAI) chat-based assistant by using Amazon Bedrock. question: A data scientist is using a prebuilt ML model in Amazon SageMaker Canvas to conduct sentiment analysis. The model predicts either positive or negative sentiment based on product review text data. The dataset is heavily imbalanced in favor of positive reviews. Which prediction metric should the data scientist use to evaluate the model?

options.text: Accuracy
options.explanation: Accuracy measures the proportion of correct predictions over all predictions, measuring how often the model makes correct predictions overall. For an imbalanced dataset that is skewed in favor of positive reviews, accuracy is not an appropriate metric. The model could predict most reviews as positive and achieve high accuracy.

options.text: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
options.explanation: RMSE is a numeric prediction metric. RMSE measures the difference between the model prediction and the actual observed values, averaged over all values that are used in the prediction. The model in this scenario is a classification model, not a regression model. Therefore, RMSE would not be an appropriate metric for evaluation.

options.text: Recall
options.explanation: Recall measures the proportion of correct positive predictions over all actual positive values. All actual positive values include both reviews that are correctly predicted as positive (true positive) and reviews that are incorrectly predicted as negative but are actually positive (false negative). To maximize recall means to minimize the false negatives.

options.text: Precision
options.explanation: Precision measures the proportion of correct positive predictions over all positive predictions. Correct positive predictions include all the reviews that are predicted as positive sentiment that are actually positive (true positive). All positive predictions include both true positives and reviews that are incorrectly predicted as positive but are actually negative (false positive). To maximize precision means to minimize false positives or cases where the model misclassifies a negative review as positive. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirements.

question: A pharmacy services company wants to build a generative AI (GenAI) application to assist pharmacists. The application must answer drug interaction questions and provide dosage guidance. question: An ML engineer uses Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to prepare a dataset for training an ML model to predict housing prices. The dataset consists of housing data from the past 10 years sorted by date and includes features such as location, size, and price. The ML engineer wants to reduce prediction bias and ensure that the model generalizes well on future, unseen data. Which SageMaker Data Wrangler split transform will meet this requirement?

options.text: Ordered split
options.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler transform ordered split maintains the order of the input data and performs a non-overlapping split among train, test, and validation, which is optional, at predefined ratios. When a timeseries dataset is sorted by date, as in this scenario, the ordered split prevents data leakage across splits by ensuring that data in the train split comes before data in the test split. This method helps reduce prediction bias and ensures the model generalizes well on future, unseen data.

options.text: Split by key
options.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler transform split by key ensures that data with the same keys do not occur in more than one split. This method is often used with id columns, so that the same id does not appear in both training and test splits. In this scenario, performing a split by key would introduce data leakage because the training data would contain samples that occurred later than some samples in the test data. This solution results in the test performance overstating the actual performance of the model and the model failing to generalize well on future, unseen data.

options.text: Randomized split
options.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler transform randomized split splits data randomly among train, test, and validation (optional) at predefined ratios. This strategy is best when you want to shuffle the order of your input data. In this scenario, randomly splitting the data would introduce data leakage because the training data would contain samples that occurred later than some samples in the test data. This method results in the test performance overstating the actual performance of the model (prediction bias), and the model failing to generalize well on future, unseen data.

options.text: Stratified split
options.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler transform stratified split splits the data among train, test, and validation (optional) such that each split is similar with respect to a specified column's categories. This method ensures that all splits have the same proportion of each category as the input dataset. Stratified split is often used for classification problems to maintain a similar percentage of samples of each target class across splits. In this scenario, performing a stratified split would introduce data leakage because the training data would contain samples that occurred later than some samples in the test data. This solution results in the test performance overstating the actual performance of the model (prediction bias), and the model failing to generalize well on future, unseen data.

question: A company deployed into production an ML model to use for image classification. The company developed a new version of the model with improved precision. The company wants to deploy the new model into production. The company must test the new model alongside the old model by using the same data. Precision cannot be compromised. Some downtime can be tolerated. Which deployment strategy will meet these requirements?

options.text: Canary deployment
options.explanation: Canary deployment would deploy the new model to a small group of users while other users continue to use the previous model. You can use canary deployment to test the new model alongside the old model. However, canary deployment does not perform inference on the same data. Additionally, this deployment strategy introduces risk because the system precision cannot be compromised.

options.text: Shadow testing
options.explanation: Shadow testing makes the new version of the model available alongside the old version. The input data runs through both versions. This strategy performs inference on the same data. This strategy ensures that the new model works as expected while minimizing risks.

options.text: A/B testing
options.explanation: An A/B testing strategy deploys changes to a model by directing a defined portion of traffic to the new model and directing the remaining traffic to the old model. This deployment strategy does not perform inference on the same data. Additionally, this strategy introduces risk because the system precision cannot be compromised.

options.text: Blue/green deployment
options.explanation: Blue/green deployment provides two identical production environments. After testing finishes on the green environment, traffic is directed from the green environment to the blue environment. A blue/green deployment strategy does not test the new model alongside the old model by using the same data.

question: An education technology company is building a learning AI assistant for students. The company uses Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for the assistant. The knowledge base course materials are organized into chapters. Each chapter covers a single topic with definitions, examples, and practice problems. However, students find that the assistant's answers are incomplete and do not fully explain the topic. Which solution will improve the quality of the assistant's responses?

options.text: Configure hierarchical chunking in the knowledge base data source configuration. Delete the existing vector index. Re-ingest the course materials.
options.explanation: The course materials have a parent-child structure. Each chapter contains definitions, examples, and practice problems for a specific topic. Hierarchical chunking creates linked parent and child chunks that preserve this structure. When retrieving a child chunk, the system replaces the child chunk with the parent chunk that contains the broader context and information. This solution resolves the issue of incomplete explanations that lack broader context.

options.text: Update the knowledge base data source chunking strategy to semantic chunking. Sync the data source.
options.explanation: Semantic chunking divides text based on semantic similarity rather than syntactic structure alone. Semantic chunking can improve chunk coherence. However, semantic chunking does not preserve the parent-child relationship between chapters and chapter content. Semantic chunking would not ensure that definitions, examples, and practice problems from the same topic link together during retrieval.

options.text: Configure a reranking model in the knowledge base. Sync the data source.
options.explanation: A reranking model reorders retrieved chunks by relevance to the user query. A reranking model can improve precision. However, reranking does not add missing context to the retrieved chunks. Reranking will not resolve the issue in the scenario if the chunks themselves lack context.

options.text: Update the knowledge base embedding model to a model with a larger vector dimension. Reindex the course materials.
options.explanation: You can increase the vector size of the embedding model to improve the semantic representation of each chunk. However, this solution does not change how the course materials are chunked. The issue is that retrieved chunks lack broader context. Therefore, the scenario describes a chunking strategy issue, not a dimensionality issue of the vector embedding.

question: An AI engineer is deploying a generative AI (GenAI) customer support chat-based application by using Amazon Bedrock. options.text: Enable sensitive information filters with custom regex patterns.
options.explanation: Sensitive information filters are designed to block or mask personally identifiable information (PII). For example, PII includes email address, date of birth, and address. Sensitive information filters use entity-based detection and custom regex patterns for structured data patterns. You would not use sensitive information filters to detect harmful content categories.

options.text: Configure content filters and set the filter strength to high for hate and violence categories.
options.explanation: Content filters detect and filter harmful content across predefined categories, including hate and violence. Each response is classified with a confidence level for each category. The confidence levels include none, low, medium, and high. You can set the filter strength to high for hate and violence to block responses classified in these categories. This configuration provides the broadest protection against harmful content reaching end users.

options.text: Create word filters by using a list of specific hateful and violent terms.
options.explanation: Word filters block specific words or phrases based on exact matches. This configuration could catch some harmful terms. However, this configuration does not detect harmful content based on confidence levels. Word filters cannot identify hate speech or violent language that has variations, context-dependent phrasing, or terms that are not explicitly listed.

options.text: Define denied topics for hate speech and violence by using sample phrases.
options.explanation: You can use denied topics to define specific topics that should be blocked in user queries or model responses. Denied topics are designed to restrict conversations to specific subject areas. Denied topics are not designed to detect and classify harmful content based on confidence levels across predefined categories such as hate and violence. Hate speech and violent language can appear across many topics and would not be reliably caught by topic-level filtering alone.

question: An AI engineer is building a legal document analysis application by using Amazon Bedrock in a single AWS Region. The application uses an Amazon Nova model.
